claim_scope_statement: Bounded schedule exploration under the bounds below is systematic concurrency testing, never proof (assurance/concurrency/plan.json claim ceiling). Native-thread stress samples schedules without coverage accounting and cannot stand in for the systematic result, nor the systematic result for native-thread evidence.

revision_note: supersedes the 7ea4780 revision after the US-017 STORY review (session 01a04626) returned BLOCK on two AC2 gaps, both now fixed at the driver/command seam: (1) BLOCKING-1 receiver-drop - dropping the sole owner (ws_core::CommandQueue) now publishes the typed CommandRefusalReason::ReceiverDropped, so a producer send after the owner is gone refuses instead of reporting accepted; the exploration probes it on EVERY schedule (79920/79920 typed refusals). (2) BLOCKING-2 dropped writes - adapter shutdown now surfaces DriverOutput::WritesDropped(DroppedWrites) accounting for every committed write it abandons, ahead of the terminal, instead of discarding them silently; the exploration checks the report against an INDEPENDENT boundary-side count of what the ended transport owed. Two new invariants (shutdown-write-drop-reported, no-write-after-shutdown) and one new named boundary fault (silent-write-drop) were added; no existing invariant was weakened and the six pre-existing minimized artifacts are byte-identical (unchanged, not refrozen). CLASSIFICATION SHIFT: the typed drop report occupies one drain poll, so 323 schedules that previously halted at a fatal Failure now reach the clean terminal instead (52924/26996 -> 53247/26673); the exclusivity assertion is unchanged and still holds on all 79920. CORRECTION CARRIED IN THIS REVISION: preregistered_plan.sha256 was stale - the recorded d73659b4... is plan.json as of 7ea4780, but plan.json changed afterwards (commits 9b8984e, 500713f), so the committed results artifact cited a digest that no tree at c680c3c had. bounds.program_shape: producer A [send_text, send_binary]; producer B [send_ping, send_close]; transport-read [inbound-ping, inbound-close, transport-eof]; transport-write [write-partial, write-all, write-all]; adapter-control [wake, shutdown]

adapter_model: the interpreter drives the public driver boundary exactly as the real adapter does: a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure HALTS the run at that instant (ws-testee io_loop maps it to LoopOutcome::ProtocolFailure and stops), so no schedule action, drain poll, or quiescence poll follows a Failure; Terminal-after-Failure is impossible by construction and additionally asserted

execution.replay_determinism: every schedule executed twice with FULL structured-trace equality: every poll record compares the input (kind + byte length), the complete typed input disposition (rejection details included), the complete command disposition (command payloads and typed rejection failures included), the complete owned output (semantic-event contents, typed failure values, byte-exact write suffixes), and the lifecycle state; the enumeration itself is re-run and compared; trace digests hash the full structured records plus the committed wire log
execution.terminal_disposition_exclusivity: asserted per run AND in aggregate: terminals total 53247 == closed_terminal_runs (exactly one each), surfaced failures total 26673 == failure_halted_runs (exactly one each, the halting failure); 53247 + 26673 == 79920

counters.reconciliation: clean-terminal runs reconcile EXACTLY per run (accepted == applied + rejected + terminal_rejected); halted runs assert at-most-once disposition of accepted commands, with commands still queued at the halt belonging to the embedding adapter's teardown (aggregate disposed 205553 of 220518 accepted; the 14965 remainder were queued at halt boundaries and never double-disposed)

execution.outcome: PASS - zero invariant violations across all 79920 schedules
execution.new_disposition_coverage: US-017 AC2 story-review dispositions are REACHED by the sweep, not only by unit fixtures: 37813 of the 79920 schedules shut down with a committed write still pending and every one of them surfaced exactly one typed DriverOutput::WritesDropped whose frames/bytes/partial_front matched the boundary's own independent count of what the ended transport owed (134430 undelivered bytes total, 4172 of the reports carrying a partially written front frame); and all 79920 schedules end with the sole owner dropped and the producer's next try_send refused with CommandRefusalReason::ReceiverDropped, never accepted

terminal_disposition_model: every full schedule reaches EXACTLY ONE typed terminal disposition, mirroring the real adapter: the clean Terminal from the absorbing Closed state (53247 runs, exactly one Terminal each, zero surfaced failures), or the halt at the first surfaced fatal Failure (26673 runs, exactly one surfaced failure each, zero Terminals) - the poisoned core retains its final state per the oracle's partial-execution semantics and the adapter stops there; both classes fully quiesce, clean-terminal runs reconcile every accepted command exactly once. The typed dropped-write disposition is NOT a third terminal: it precedes the Terminal in the same run and is scored only on non-halted runs, since a halted adapter stops at its Failure

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: this exploration, first execution against the batch-C driver
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll latched eof_applied=true even when the core refused the TransportEof with its NON-FATAL backpressure code (event queue congested), permanently losing the EOF: the connection stayed in Closing forever and no terminal was ever delivered
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: the EOF now stays latched on a non-fatal refusal and is retried on the next quiescent turn after outputs drain; fatal refusals still surface as a Failure output and latch
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: both regression tests were executed against the pre-fix driver (fix stashed) and their failures were read; both pass with the fix restored

defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: closure-commit review session 01a04533; reproduced RED by asserting terminal/failure exclusivity on the pre-fix interpreter
defects_found_and_fixed.description: the exploration interpreter kept driving a run after a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure, so schedules such as the minimized `shutdown,inbound-close` recorded BOTH a fatal Failure and a later Terminal while passing, invalidating the exclusive disposition oracle and the prior 732-run classification
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: adapter-faithful stop-on-Failure in the interpreter (no further schedule actions, drain, or quiescence polls after a Failure) plus the failure-halt-exclusivity invariant; the schedule space was reclassified and re-counted (52924 clean-terminal / 26996 failure-halted)
defects_found_and_fixed.note: harness fix, not a driver change; the shipped driver passes the corrected oracle on all schedules

defects_found_and_fixed.finding_verbatim: AC2 lacks a typed receiver-drop outcome; sends can return accepted after the sole owner has been dropped.
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ws_core::CommandSender::try_send returned Ok(()) after the sole owner (CommandQueue, held by ConnectionDriver) was dropped, admitting the command into a bounded queue that no owner would ever drain. The prior US-017 closure pinned that acceptance as CORRECT (driver_contract.rs: expect("capacity admits one command even with the owner gone")), so the gap was actively locked in by a test.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: CommandChannel carries a receiver_dropped flag set by Drop for CommandQueue while it HOLDS the queue lock; try_send reads it inside the same lock, so the flag and the push are decided in one critical section and no send can be accepted past a receiver that is going away. The refusal uses the incumbent refusal vocabulary (new CommandRefusalReason::ReceiverDropped), not a parallel mechanism, and is terminal for the channel.
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: read on the pre-fix driver: `a send after the sole owner is dropped must never report accepted: ()` - the `()` is the Ok(()) the send actually returned

defects_found_and_fixed.finding_verbatim: AC2 silently abandons committed pending writes on adapter shutdown instead of reporting the required typed dropped-write disposition.
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll(DriverInput::Shutdown) discarded the offered write and drained the core's remaining wire writes with `while self.core.next_write().is_some() {}` - correct to abort, but nothing was reported, so a producer that had already seen CommandDisposition::Applied was left believing bytes it will never see were sent
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: abort_pending_writes accounts every abandoned committed write into a DroppedWrites{frames,bytes,partial_front} report surfaced as DriverOutput::WritesDropped ahead of DriverOutput::Terminal; next_output re-sweeps on every post-shutdown poll so a write appearing after shutdown would be aborted and reported too rather than offered to a dead transport
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: read on the pre-fix driver: `the abandoned committed suffix is reported, not silently dropped: ["event", "event", "event", "event", "terminal"]` / left: Some("event") right: Some("writes-dropped:frames=1,bytes=3,partial_front=true")

retention.mechanism: any failing schedule is shrunk by a deterministic greedy delta-debug loop to a 1-minimal failing schedule (every single-action removal verified non-failing) and persisted as a key=value seed artifact recording property, mutation, event-queue capacity, schedule, and counterexample
retention.real_failure_path: retain_and_fail writes fuzz-seeds/us017/minimized/retained-<property>.seed and fails the suite with the artifact path and minimized schedule
retention.demonstration: seven named boundary faults (the six-fault mutation vocabulary adopted with attribution from codex-import 6a7606a fuzz-seeds/us017/*.seed, plus silent-write-drop added by this revision for the story-review BLOCKING-2 behavior) are each injected at the test-only public driver boundary; the exploration detects every one, the shrinker minimizes it, fault-localization is verified (minimized schedule passes clean, fails faulted), and the minimized artifact is pinned byte-for-byte
retention.regeneration: US017_RETAIN=1 is the sanctioned deliberate-refreeze path; the pinned replay otherwise compares committed bytes; a corpus mutex serializes writer and reader tests

native_stress.suite: rust/ws-driver/tests/concurrency.rs (pre-existing batch-C native-thread stress, unchanged by this closure): 4 producer threads x 50 commands exactly-once with full wire reconciliation, and terminal-exactly-once under racing producers across a shutdown

limitations: not a formal proof or exhaustive full-state-space result: exhaustive ONLY within the declared 5-program/12-action alphabet and context-switch bound 7
modeled schedules serialize all actors through the owner's poll; they establish no native-thread evidence (no real preemption timing, weak-memory visibility, or OS scheduling)
native-thread stress executed on this darwin arm64 host only: no Linux or second blocking-platform execution, so the story's two-platform runtime claim (AC4) remains open
no Loom, Miri, or TSAN execution (zero-dependency gate; the exploration harness is hand-built against the sans-io core)

the event-queue capacity used is 8, not the config floor 4: ConnectionCore::byte_input_event_bound needs 6 free slots to admit even a one-frame chunk, so floor-4 configurations can never make byte-path progress (recorded as an open config-floor observation, not changed by this closure)
no live Java executed; no Java-equivalence claim

max_dropped_frames_in_one_report is 1 across all 79920 schedules, and that is structural rather than lucky: next_output moves a committed write into the offered slot as soon as one exists, and no command, inbound chunk, or EOF is applied while a write is offered, so at most one committed write is pending at any shutdown instant. The plural accumulation in abort_pending_writes is therefore a guarantee, not an exercised path; it is pinned by driver_contract.rs::no_committed_write_survives_or_appears_after_the_shutdown_report rather than by a multi-frame observation

assurance/concurrency/plan.json is preregistered and was NOT edited by this revision, so its action vocabulary still names neither a dropped-write outcome under action.shutdown (SHUTDOWN_IDEMPOTENT, LATE_CONNECTION_GOING_AWAY, DRAIN_WINDOW_BOUNDED) nor any receiver-drop action at all. The two AC2 dispositions added here are therefore evidenced by the exploration and the unit suites, not by the preregistered action model
